result.summary: golang.org/x/sync/errgroup is a small goroutine-synchronization library that uses only context, fmt and sync from the standard library. I checked the whole file for init code, network or file access, process execution, encoded payloads and runtime patching and found none. The NETWORK capability is a transitive standard-library attribution, not real network use.

findings.title: Standard errgroup implementation, no side effects
findings.detail: The file matches upstream errgroup: Group, WithContext, Wait, Go, TryGo and SetLimit. It imports only context, fmt and sync. It has no init functions, no build steps, no encoded data, no file or network access and no runtime hooking.

capabilities.explanation: No direct network use. errgroup imports only context, fmt and sync. Capslock attributes NETWORK conservatively through transitive standard-library edges, such as the context package or fmt's interface-based formatting reaching net types, or through calls to caller-supplied functions in Go/TryGo. The package itself opens no connections.
